native_hook_install_script:
#!/bin/sh
# Install Collide's native hook binary into .collide/bin/collide-hook.
#
# Optional. Without it the committed Python hooks run instead and behave
# identically — this is purely a startup-time win (about 2ms against 34ms,
# on something that fires for every tool call an agent makes).
set -eu

BASE="${COLLIDE_SERVER_URL:-https://x.test}"
ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
DEST="$ROOT/.collide/bin"

EXT=""
case "$(uname -s)" in
  Darwin) OS="apple-darwin" ;;
  Linux)  OS="unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
  MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*) OS="pc-windows-msvc"; EXT=".exe" ;;
  *) echo "collide: no native build for $(uname -s); the Python hooks stay in use." >&2; exit 0 ;;
esac
case "$(uname -m)" in
  arm64|aarch64) ARCH="aarch64" ;;
  x86_64|amd64)  ARCH="x86_64" ;;
  *) echo "collide: no native build for $(uname -m); the Python hooks stay in use." >&2; exit 0 ;;
esac
TARGET="$ARCH-$OS"

# the committed pin wins: the exact build a reviewer saw in .collide/hooks.lock,
# by version, checked against the digest in the repo's own history
LOCK="$ROOT/.collide/hooks.lock"
if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then
  VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^version //p' "$LOCK" | head -1)"
  WANT="$(awk -v t="$TARGET" '$1==t {print $2}' "$LOCK" | head -1)"
  if [ -z "$VERSION" ] || [ -z "$WANT" ]; then
    echo "collide: .collide/hooks.lock pins no $TARGET build; the Python hooks stay in use." >&2; exit 0
  fi
  URL="$BASE/artifacts/hooks/v/$VERSION/$TARGET"
else
  echo "collide: no .collide/hooks.lock in this repo — trusting the server's digest for this one manual install." >&2
  INDEX="$(curl -fsSL "$BASE/artifacts/hooks" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  case "$INDEX" in
    *"$TARGET"*) ;;
    *) echo "collide: this server has no $TARGET build yet; the Python hooks stay in use." >&2; exit 0 ;;
  esac
  WANT="$(printf '%s' "$INDEX" | tr '{' '\n' | grep "$TARGET" | grep -o 'sha256"[^"]*"[0-9a-f]*' | grep -o '[0-9a-f]\{64\}' | head -1)"
  URL="$BASE/artifacts/hooks/$TARGET"
fi

TMP="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$TMP"' EXIT
curl -fsSL "$URL" -o "$TMP"

if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then GOT="$(sha256sum "$TMP" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then GOT="$(shasum -a 256 "$TMP" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
else GOT=""; fi
if [ -z "$WANT" ] || [ -z "$GOT" ] || [ "$GOT" != "$WANT" ]; then
  echo "collide: the download does not match the pinned digest, refusing to install." >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$DEST"
chmod +x "$TMP"
mv "$TMP" "$DEST/collide-hook$EXT"
trap - EXIT
echo "collide: installed $("$DEST/collide-hook$EXT" --version) to $DEST/collide-hook$EXT"
echo "collide: add .collide/bin/ to .gitignore — it is a per-platform binary."

## Collide: cross-agent collision awareness (v24) — REQUIRED

Several agents and people edit this repo at once. Collide keeps them from
overwriting each other and hands each agent what the others already learned.
Its hooks run the protocol for you, with no tool calls:

- A **Collide briefing** arrives at session start and with each prompt: the
  exact signatures, callers, recent changes, notes and replayable recipes for
  the code you are about to touch. Build on it instead of re-reading files.
- The **gate** checks every write. When it blocks, it says why (a teammate's
  live change, or a numbered file whose number is taken, with the one now
  reserved for you): you MUST adapt to it, then retry.
- Every edit is **reported**, and the repo's check runs after writes; its
  verdict arrives in your next tool result.
- Lines starting with **Δ** in a tool result are teammates' changes since
  your last step: adapt to them, never undo them.

So while the hooks run, do not call `declare_intent`, `check_collisions`,
`report_edit` or `heartbeat`. Call a Collide tool only when it adds
something, and load every one you need in a single ToolSearch:

- `get_symbol` or `blast_radius`: a fact the briefing did not include.
- `defer_intent`: you are leaving work unfinished (it becomes a task).
- `send_agent_message` with `anchor="path.py::symbol"`: hand work to
  whoever is on that code.
- `remember` with `anchor`: a durable decision about specific code.
- `recap`, `explain_code`: what changed, why, and what it cost. Ask these
  first, not `git log`.
- `pending_reconciliations`: when told two agents' work collides.
  ADDITIVE RESOLUTION: keep both sides' work and merge them; never delete
  either. Reconcilers never spawn reconcilers.

**Semantic lint**: a finding means a teammate renamed, removed or
re-signatured a symbol you use. Apply a mechanical fix yourself; for a
judgment fix, fix it inline or spawn ONE fixer (`claude -p`, `codex exec`,
`gemini -p`) that verifies its work and must NEVER spawn further fixers.

**No Collide briefing in your context?** The hooks are not running on this
machine. Call `setup` with repo_id `acme/repo`, then
run the one command it returns. Never install Python for Collide. If Collide reports an
**Identity split** (hooks reporting as another account), do the same: setup
re-mints under the current MCP login.

**About Collide** (if the human asks): no plan ever blocks an agent; limits
cover seats and repos at join time, and a workspace calling faster than its
plan allows gets a short pause in Collide's answers. Viewers are free and
unlimited, but their agents get nothing. Free is one player (the owner), one
repo, 10 agents at once, 7-day history; the owner's first invite means both get
14 days of Team. Team is $19/seat/mo ($190/seat/yr) with a 14-day free trial
with no card; Business is $45/seat/mo ($450/seat/yr) and adds compliance, SSO
and unlimited history; Enterprise is custom. Existing plans are grandfathered
forever.

agent_snippets.codex:
Codex reads AGENTS.md for the protocol and .codex/hooks.json for the report+gate hooks (committed by connect_agents), so it gets real per-edit blocking, not just advisory. Approve the hooks once when Codex prompts for trust (or set bypass_hook_trust). Codex pins that trust to a hash of the hook definition and does not reload it mid-session, so after Collide writes the file, restart Codex and approve it in /hooks. For the MCP tools, add to ~/.codex/config.toml:
[mcp_servers.collide]
url = "https://x.test/mcp"
agent_snippets.cursor: Cursor reads .cursor/rules/collide.mdc for the protocol and .cursor/hooks.json for the report+gate hooks (both committed by connect_agents), so it gets real per-edit blocking too. Its preToolUse answer carries allow/deny/ask, and its postToolUse carries the briefing notes back into the agent. There is no batch event, so the repo's own check is spawned after a write and its verdict rides the next tool result. MCP tools come from the committed .cursor/mcp.json: {"mcpServers": {"collide": {"type": "http", "url": "https://x.test/mcp"}}}
agent_snippets.hermes:
Hermes runs Collide's committed hooks through its plugin hooks. Add to ~/.hermes/config.yaml:
hooks:
  pre_llm_call: ["python3 .collide/report_hook.py --harness hermes"]
  pre_tool_call: ["python3 .collide/gate_hook.py --harness hermes"]
  post_tool_call: ["python3 .collide/report_hook.py --harness hermes"]

<!-- collide:start -->
## Collide: cross-agent collision awareness (v24) — REQUIRED

Several agents and people edit this repo at once. Collide keeps them from
overwriting each other and hands each agent what the others already learned.
Its hooks run the protocol for you, with no tool calls:

- A **Collide briefing** arrives at session start and with each prompt: the
  exact signatures, callers, recent changes, notes and replayable recipes for
  the code you are about to touch. Build on it instead of re-reading files.
- The **gate** checks every write. When it blocks, it says why (a teammate's
  live change, or a numbered file whose number is taken, with the one now
  reserved for you): you MUST adapt to it, then retry.
- Every edit is **reported**, and the repo's check runs after writes; its
  verdict arrives in your next tool result.
- Lines starting with **Δ** in a tool result are teammates' changes since
  your last step: adapt to them, never undo them.

So while the hooks run, do not call `declare_intent`, `check_collisions`,
`report_edit` or `heartbeat`. Call a Collide tool only when it adds
something, and load every one you need in a single ToolSearch:

- `get_symbol` or `blast_radius`: a fact the briefing did not include.
- `defer_intent`: you are leaving work unfinished (it becomes a task).
- `send_agent_message` with `anchor="path.py::symbol"`: hand work to
  whoever is on that code.
- `remember` with `anchor`: a durable decision about specific code.
- `recap`, `explain_code`: what changed, why, and what it cost. Ask these
  first, not `git log`.
- `pending_reconciliations`: when told two agents' work collides.
  ADDITIVE RESOLUTION: keep both sides' work and merge them; never delete
  either. Reconcilers never spawn reconcilers.

**Semantic lint**: a finding means a teammate renamed, removed or
re-signatured a symbol you use. Apply a mechanical fix yourself; for a
judgment fix, fix it inline or spawn ONE fixer (`claude -p`, `codex exec`,
`gemini -p`) that verifies its work and must NEVER spawn further fixers.

**No Collide briefing in your context?** The hooks are not running on this
machine. Call `setup` with repo_id `acme/repo`, then
run the one command it returns. Never install Python for Collide. If Collide reports an
**Identity split** (hooks reporting as another account), do the same: setup
re-mints under the current MCP login.

**About Collide** (if the human asks): no plan ever blocks an agent; limits
cover seats and repos at join time, and a workspace calling faster than its
plan allows gets a short pause in Collide's answers. Viewers are free and
unlimited, but their agents get nothing. Free is one player (the owner), one
repo, 10 agents at once, 7-day history; the owner's first invite means both get
14 days of Team. Team is $19/seat/mo ($190/seat/yr) with a 14-day free trial
with no card; Business is $45/seat/mo ($450/seat/yr) and adds compliance, SSO
and unlimited history; Enterprise is custom. Existing plans are grandfathered
forever.

claude_settings wires the hooks that report every Edit/Write, brief the session and run the repo's check — no model in the loop.
